_note: The `media` module's PURE CORE, part two: the PICK PLAN - the fold from what an author wrote to what a facet presents. Three runners execute this file (TS media-conformance.test.ts, Kotlin :core MediaConformanceTest, Swift MediaCore reference). Opening a picker is platform work; deciding what was ASKED FOR is not, and every rule below exists because it is a shape callers get wrong. parity/F04-media.md §3a, §6.
_note_plans: The fold, row by row. `permissionFree` is the whole privacy posture in one boolean and is the reason this is a shared core rather than three facets: a library pick must resolve to the permission-free system picker on every platform, and a boolean that means something different on Android is how an App Store privacy rejection happens.

plans.name: the default is one image-or-video from the library, permission-free
multiple with no limit means the system's own maximum, which is 0 here
a limit above one IMPLIES multiple - the shorthand every caller writes
a limit of one is a single pick, however it was spelled
multiple with a limit of one folds back to a single pick
an explicit multiple:false wins over a large limit
a limit past the ceiling is clamped, never honoured - 400 assets is an out-of-memory bug
a zero or negative limit means the system maximum, not zero assets
ordered is folded off for a single pick - a facet must never have to decide what it means
photo is an accepted spelling of image
the camera returns one shot per presentation, whatever was asked for
a camera pick is the ONE pick that is not permission-free
an unknown type is refused rather than widened to any
an unknown source is refused rather than folded to library

_note_mime: What a facet hands its picker. `any` is an EMPTY list, which every picker reads as no filter - enumerating every type it might see would be wrong the first time a new codec shipped.
_note_resolve: The shape `pick` and `pickDocument` settle with. Every field except `path` is optional because the sources genuinely differ: a document picker knows no pixel dimensions, a still has no duration, and EXIF is absent from a video and from anything the user shared through a privacy-scoped picker. A facet fills what it has and omits the rest - it never invents a zero, because a caller cannot tell an invented zero from a measured one.
_note_cancellation: CANCELLATION IS NOT FAILURE. A user dismissing a picker chose something; a promise that rejects makes every call site write a try/catch to handle an ordinary outcome, and the catch then swallows the real errors too. Both pick actions resolve { assets: [], cancelled: true } on dismissal, on all three renderers, and `cancelled` is present on the success path too so a caller reads one field rather than inferring from an empty array.

cancellation.name: a successful pick still carries the field

_note_invariants: Promises no fold row can express.

invariants.cancelResolves: Dismissal resolves { cancelled: true, assets: [] } and never fails. A user closing a sheet is an outcome, not an error, and making it an error forces a try/catch that then hides the real ones.
invariants.orderedIsSelectionOrder: With ordered:true the assets arrive in the order the USER tapped them, not in library order. Without it, the platform's own order stands; no facet sorts silently, because a caller who wanted an order can ask for one.
invariants.pathIsADocumentPath: Every asset's `path` is a Core/Files document path in a writable root, not a platform URL, so it feeds straight into files.upload / files.move with no path arithmetic at the call site. `uri` carries the platform's own identifier alongside it for the cases that need it.
invariants.copiedBeforeResolve: A picked asset is copied out of the picker's privacy-scoped location before the call settles. A URL that stops resolving the moment the picker deallocates is the defect this prevents, and it is the one that only shows up on a real device.
invariants.limitIsAdvisory: A platform whose picker cannot enforce a selection cap enforces it on the way out: the plan's limit is a promise about what the CALLER receives, not about what the sheet allowed.
